## Why

The chosen subject is a single, large, ornate bell, which historically calls religious communities together and regulates monastic life. This concrete object perfectly captures *Ubi Primum’s* purpose: Pope Pius IX is sounding a clear "alarm" to the heads of all religious orders, commanding them to rouse their members to renewal and necessary reform. A bell was selected because it is universally recognized as a tool of collective awakening, discipline, and unity, avoiding the vagueness of abstract geometry while directly embodying the encyclical's call for order, revitalization, and obedience.

## Text-to-image prompt

A single, monumental, highly-detailed religious church bell rendered as a premium sculptural object on a transparent background. The sculpture is a dead-center, frontal, orthographic visualization of a grand bronze bell, standing approximately 1.5 meters tall on a simple, dark patinated bronze plinth. The bell itself is cast from rich, aged, gold-patinated bronze with visible procedural microtextures, surface imperfections, and subtle weathering. The elaborate crown is formed into intricate sculptural loops (cannons) that resolve into stylized lion heads. The main body of the bell is adorned with rich, high-relief sculpted borders of acanthus leaves and delicate cross motifs, executed with physically based material accuracy. A heavy bronze clapper hangs visibly within the dark interior. The sculpture rests symmetrically on the dark, heavy bronze plinth, centered in the frame. Lighting is dramatic chiaroscuro: a strong, focused key light from the front-left creates sharp specular highlights on the ornate reliefs and deep shadows across the bell's curves. Pronounced ambient occlusion defines the depths of all relief carvings. The render is extremely detailed, resembling a luxury Houdini or Cinema 4D visualization with ray-traced reflections and physically based lighting. There is generous negative space around the isolated bell. The composition is perfectly symmetrical with no tilt or angle. No text, inscriptions, or readable lettering appear on any surface of the bell or plinth.
